reasons: It is already the lease consumed by CandidateFeatureGpuBatchRequestV1.
It binds the real owner-process CUDA residency observation into GPU_RESIDENT ArtifactAddressV1 values.
It carries candidateSnapshotRevision, ordinalMapChecksum, featureSnapshotChecksum, columnarChecksum, workspaceRevision, featureRevision and gpuPackChecksum lineage.
It binds deviceId/deviceName, host staging mode, opaque buffer IDs, source checksums and materialized resident checksums without exposing pointers or CUDA IPC.
It emits a separate release receipt instead of making a released lease look reusable.

evidenceWorthPreserving: No identity authority or canonical writes.
notCanonicalBecause: No batch-request consumer uses this schema.
It does not carry columnarChecksum, workspaceRevision, featureRevision or deviceName lineage present in the canonical owner.
It was independently built and never cross-referenced with the existing residency owner.

invariants: CandidateOrdinal remains snapshot-scoped execution identity, not canonical identity.
GPU residency remains a reconstructible performance layer.
ArtifactAddressV1 is a location/reference contract, not semantic authority.
Resident reuse must be bound to exact lease/checksum/revision identity.
No raw CUDA pointer or allocator-class name becomes an Atlas identifier.
cuTile, CUDA SIMT, cuVS and cuGraph remain executor implementations behind later promotion gates.
